# Write a clean subject on the first line, without a label prefix.
# Start with a capitalized action verb. Aim for 50 characters.
# Leave a blank line before the body. Wrap body text at 72 characters.
Subject

Why:

How:

Tags:

# Why, How and Tags are all required.
# Why: say why this change is needed.
# How: say how it addresses that need. Keep claims within the evidence.
#
# Tags: Bug, Enhancement.
# Choose any that apply, including both Bug and Enhancement when both apply.
# Use None alone when none fits. All other labels stay out.
# Tags belong in the body, not before the subject.
#
# Never put private conversation references, secrets or personal details here.
# Delete prompts and comments from the finished message.
#
# These verbs are choices, not words every commit must contain:
# Create = Introduce something new, like a feature, test or dependency.
# Remove = Take out something that exists, like a feature, test or dependency.
# Fix = Repair something broken, like a defect, typo or wrong statement.
# Bump = Raise the version of a component, like a dependency.
# Build = Change how the project gets built, its tooling or infrastructure.
# Enable = Switch on an existing feature or setting.
# Disable = Switch off an existing feature or setting while keeping it.
# Optimize = Improve performance only, like faster code.
# Document = Touch documentation only, like help files.
# Refactor = Restructure code without changing what it does.
# Reformat = Change layout only, like indentation or spacing.
# Rephrase = Change wording only, like a comment or doc line.
